children: Shares in life-sciences investor Syncona rose after portfolio company Beacon Therapeutics said a gene therapy for a disease that causes blindness achieved positive results in a pivotal study.
Shares in Syncona were up 5.8% in European morning trading Monday, taking their year-to-date gain to around 24%.

Beacon said its laruparetigene zovaparvovec--or laru-zova--therapy met the primary goal in a mid- and late-stage clinical trial for X-linked retinitis pigmentosa, an inherited retinal disease. The study showed patients who underwent the therapy demonstrated improvements in the number of letters they could read in a test with dim light.
The company said the drug had a favorable safety and tolerability profile in the trial, consistent with prior studies.

Syncona acquired Applied Genetic Technologies in 2022 and formed Beacon with laru-zova as the lead asset. The investor said it has a 38.4% stake in Beacon and that its holding was valued at 183.4 million pounds ($245.7 million) as of June 30.
Beacon Chief Executive Lance Baldo said the company would work closely with regulatory authorities to bring laru-zova to patients as quickly as possible.
